prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right one depends on your income, health needs, budget, whether you want marketplace (ACA) plans, an HSA‑eligible plan, or a small‑business/owner plan (QSEHRA, SHOP), and whether you prefer a local agent you can meet in person or an online broker.

How to find the best broker for you
- Look for an independent agent/broker who can quote both ACA marketplace plans and off‑exchange plans (gives you more choices).  
- Verify they’re licensed in Missouri (Missouri Dept. of Insurance) and have experience with self‑employed clients and subsidies.  
- Prefer someone who is marketplace‑certified if you need help with premium tax credits.  
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and ask for client references.  
- Ask about fees — many agents are paid by carriers, but some charge a client fee for consulting.

Places to search right now
- Healthcare.gov agent/broker locator (works during Open Enrollment and year‑round for off‑exchange agents).  
- National online brokers: HealthSherpa and eHealth are easy for quotes and enrollment; Stride Health focuses on freelancers/independent workers. (Pros: fast quotes; cons: less personalized/local help.)  
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” tool for local certified brokers.  
- Missouri Dept. of Commerce & Insurance agent lookup to confirm license and complaints.

Questions to ask any broker before you sign on
- Do you work with self‑employed clients and help with ACA subsidy eligibility?  
- Can you enroll me in marketplace plans and explain premium tax credits?  
- Will you compare HSA‑eligible high‑deductible plans if I want an HSA?  
- Do you help set up QSEHRA or other small‑employer health reimbursement arrangements?  
- How are you compensated? Any client fees?  
- Can you provide references from other self‑employed clients?

Next step I can take for you
If you tell me your ZIP code and a few priorities (monthly budget, whether you want HSA, whether you expect to qualify for premium tax credits, need for in‑person meetings), I’ll find 3–5 Kansas City, MO brokers/agents (with contact info and recent ratings) who match your needs and list pros/cons for each.
